assumptions: Chemical data retrieved from ChEMBL and PubChem databases
Site classification based on CovInDB dataset for KRAS (P01116)
Orthosteric vs allosteric determination using protein family-specific rules
Residue frequency analysis performed on all KRAS covalent inhibitor entries

conclusions.finding: Sotorasib and Adagrasib are both approved drugs with similar physicochemical profiles
conclusions.implication: Both compounds show drug-like properties suitable for oral bioavailability

conclusions.finding: All 286 KRAS covalent inhibitors target the orthosteric CYS-12 site
conclusions.implication: CYS-12 represents the dominant and highly druggable hotspot for KRAS G12C inhibition

conclusions.finding: No allosteric covalent inhibitors identified in the dataset
conclusions.implication: Opportunity exists for discovering novel allosteric covalent KRAS modulators

conclusions.finding: 100% targeting of a single cysteine residue (CYS-12)
conclusions.implication: KRAS G12C covalent drug discovery is highly focused on mutation-specific targeting

recommendations: Sotorasib and Adagrasib represent validated chemical starting points for KRAS G12C inhibition
CYS-12 should be prioritized as the primary covalent warhead attachment site for KRAS G12C
Explore allosteric covalent inhibitor opportunities to diversify KRAS targeting strategies
Investigate other cysteine residues in KRAS for potential alternative covalent binding sites
Consider non-G12C KRAS mutants that may have alternative druggable cysteines
